title: Design systems: put the brand into practice
summary: Reuse components, rules and assets across the product.
why: Shared rules reduce repeated design and development.
Complete component states let agents extend pages while preserving usability and brand consistency.
know: Tokens define color, type, spacing and motion. Components define usage, states and behavior.
Brand assets need versions, licenses, formats and usage rules.
Implement the rules in code and test them with real content.
inputs: Approved brand direction, logo, fonts and asset licenses
Existing libraries, page types, content and language needs
actions: Audit repeated styles and create semantic tokens and a component inventory.
Define interaction and responsive behavior for buttons, forms, navigation and content modules.
Deliver working components, example pages and a version history from a shared source.
done: Long and short content, narrow screens and error states work.
Design and code share token values; assets have valid usage rights.
pitfalls: Inventing new type scales and buttons for every page.
Delivering assets without checking their licenses.
decision: Approve the visual direction and shared rules before extending the interface.

reader.concept: A design system gives the team shared colors, type, components and interaction rules so pages feel consistent.
reader.when: Use this when the site grows, more people contribute or similar components keep being rebuilt.

example.situation: Three pages use different primary-button colors, sizes and error messages.
example.lesson: Shared rules let you update them together.

reader.first_step: Start with buttons, forms and text hierarchy.
terms: A shared style value, such as a color or spacing size.
A reusable interface element with states and behavior.
